tagline.text: One of the Philippines' largest marine parks, beside SM Seaside

location.label: Location
location.text: Beside the SM Seaside complex, F. Vestil Street, South Road Properties (SRP), Cebu City

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (mostly indoor; outdoor areas best in the dry season)

children.text: Cebu Ocean Park is a marine theme park that opened in 2019 beside the SM Seaside complex in Cebu City's SRP district. It combines a large oceanarium with a 360-degree tunnel, a jungle trek, a lorikeet aviary, and a fur seal show in one place. Many exhibits are indoors and work in the rain, so it is a regular stop for families with children.
Cebu Ocean Park is a marine theme park right beside the SM Seaside complex in SRP (South Road Properties), a reclaimed area south of Cebu City. According to SunStar, it held a media tour on
August 23
, 2019, a soft opening on
August 24
, and a grand opening on
October 1
, billing itself as the largest oceanarium in the Philippines at the time. It is reported to belong to the same group as Manila Ocean Park.
The centerpiece is the Deep Tank Lagoon, a large tank about

deep holding roughly 3,500 cubic meters of water. Walking through the 360-degree tunnel beneath it, you pass reef sharks, eagle rays, and schools of tropical fish above and on both sides. The park also includes the open-air Jungle Trek and Creepy Critters (reptile and insect displays), the Lory Loft where birds fly freely, and the blue-lit Seven Seas gallery.
The site is reported to cover about 1.5 hectares, so it is not an all-day mega theme park. Strolling at an easy pace and following the show schedule takes about
3–4 hours

. Stingray Interaction, Sea Trek (helmet diving), and the Crocodile Cage Experience cost extra, so decide in advance what the base ticket covers and which activities to pay for, and your budget will stay on track.

The location is another plus. Across the road is the large SM Seaside City mall, with restaurants, money changers, and a supermarket, so you can follow the park with a meal and shopping in one trip. It is easy to reach from downtown Cebu and from the Mactan airport side, making it a good half-day stop in the middle of a Cebu City itinerary.

blocks.title: Deep Tank Lagoon and the 360-degree tunnel

children.text: This is the heart of the park. In the tunnel running through a tank about
deep and holding roughly 3,500 cubic meters of water, you see reef sharks, eagle rays, and schools of tropical fish above, below, and beside you. It is liveliest at feeding time.

An air-conditioned indoor gallery with blue lighting, where you can see reef fish, garden eels, and more up close. It is a good place to cool off at midday and one of the spots where children linger longest.

A space where lorikeets fly freely. If you hold a cup of nectar, the birds may land on your hand or shoulder. Bird feeding costs extra, and the suspended wooden bridge section cannot be used with wheelchairs or strollers.

These are the open-air zones near the entrance. Jungle Trek shows freshwater and large river fish, while Creepy Critters has reptiles, amphibians, and insects such as Burmese pythons, monitor lizards, and sugar gliders. They are coolest early in the morning.

blocks.title: Fur seal show and bird show

children.text: The amphitheater hosts a fur seal show and a bird show at set times. The bird show and the main tank feeding run at the same times, so you must pick one. The fur seal show falls between them and never overlaps. Outdoor shows may be delayed or canceled if there is lightning.
Stingray Interaction lasts about
30 minutes
, and Sea Trek lets you walk on the tank floor wearing a helmet. Sea Trek is limited to ages 8 and up and a height of at least
140cm
, and you must not fly for 12 hours afterward, so avoid it on your departure day.

items.title: Basic half-day route
items.subtitle: A weekday plan timed to opening

children.text: Enter at opening, go through the turnstiles with your QR e-ticket, and start with Jungle Trek and Creepy Critters while it is coolest.
Take photos with the birds at the Lory Loft. If you want to feed them, pay at the counter now.
Cool off in the air-conditioned Seven Seas gallery while watching the tropical fish.
Walk slowly through the 360-degree tunnel of the Deep Tank Lagoon. The crowds have not arrived yet, so it is a good time for photos.
Have lunch at the food hall inside the park. A meal is reported at around
Take a seat in the main tank feeding stands 15–20 minutes early. It overlaps with the bird show at the same time, so choose one.
Watch the fur seal show, then use the remaining time for a paid activity such as Stingray Interaction.

Show times are listed as 11:00, 13:00, and 15:00 for the bird show and main tank feeding, and 12:00, 14:00, and 16:00 for the fur seal show, but they may change, so check the signboard when you enter.

The park sits beside the SM Seaside complex in SRP, so you can stay near SM Seaside, in downtown Cebu City, or in the Mactan resort area and travel back and forth easily. For families, hotels around SRP and the nearby malls are convenient, and many people also stay on Mactan near the airport and make the trip in one go by taxi or Grab.

The park has a food hall where a meal costs around ₱200–400, and there is also mention of a reservation-only upscale restaurant next to the glass tunnel. Outside food is reported to be restricted at the bag check, so it is better to eat at the restaurants and food court of SM Seaside across the road after you leave. A personal tumbler is said to be allowed, so fill it with water before going in.
Going on a weekday right at opening is coolest and least crowded. Entry is reported to stop about an hour before closing, so avoid the late afternoon.
Online booking is generally cheaper than buying at the gate. With a QR e-ticket, you can skip the ticket booth and go straight to the turnstiles.
Once you leave through the turnstiles, you cannot re-enter and the ticket becomes void. Eat lunch inside or finish all the exhibits before you go out.
The bird show and main tank feeding run at the same time, so you can watch only one. The feeding stands fill up fast, so sit 15–20 minutes early.
For Stingray Interaction or Sea Trek, bring a towel and a change of clothes, and plan not to fly for 12 hours after a Sea Trek.
Flash photography is banned at all exhibits. Turn off the flash on your phone.
The park is said not to rent strollers or wheelchairs, so bring your own. Only the suspended wooden bridge in the Lory Loft is closed to wheels.
Large suitcases may not fit in the lockers inside the park, so use the baggage counters at SM Seaside.
Tickets are non-refundable and there is no re-entry once you exit the turnstiles. Prices, operating hours, and show times change often, so check official notices before you go.
Prices and hours differ by source. The opening-period weekday price of about ₱600 appears as about ₱800 in recent reviews, so check the latest announcement.
Tickets are said to be non-refundable even in bad weather or typhoons, so choose your date carefully when the forecast is poor.
Some travelers feel uneasy about animal performances such as the fur seal show. Decide whether to watch according to your own values.
The park states that it will not keep dolphins or whales. Follow staff instructions at every animal activity, and do not touch the animals or feed them on your own.
On weekends and holidays the parking lot fills early and the lines get long. Allow extra travel time.
A large mall right across from the park. With restaurants, a food court, a supermarket, and money changers, it is handy before or after your visit, and it is a
5–10 minute
walk away.
About
15–20 minutes
by taxi from the park, downtown holds leading sights such as Magellan's Cross and the Basilica del Santo Niño.
A business and commercial district full of cafés and restaurants,
20–30 minutes
from SRP by car. It is a popular choice for dinner.
A large mall in Cebu Business Park, a good place to continue with shopping or a meal after the park.
